messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about the streaming queue adapter boundary we sketched. I worry we left the admission logic in two places (adapter + scheduler) which will create subtle latency regressions when adapters prefetch aggressively. Thoughts?
lee: yeah spotted that too. If adapter prefetches and scheduler also enforces headroom we can double-count capacity and either overfill GPU or starve small requests.
ankur: can you sketch the two options? push vs pull?
maria: sure. Option A: adapter is dumb — only normalizes request shape, emits admission requests to scheduler which owns all headroom, credit accounting, eviction. Option B: adapter does soft-admit (prefetch up to N), scheduler does hard admit; adapter can drop prefetched items if headroom revoked.
jessica: Option B feels performant but adds complexity (revocation paths). How often will revokes happen in steady-state?
lee: depends on tenant churn; on multi-tenant GPUs revokes would be rare if scheduler maintains conservative estimates. But bursts from small-latency tenants could cause frequent revokes.
ankur: revokes are painful because they break KV cache warmup and stream continuity. If adapter throws away prefetched tokens we lose most benefit.
oliver: thought: what if adapter maintains a tiny local budget (soft credits) that must be replenished by the scheduler on longer cadence? So adapter can prefetch a few microbatches for throughput, but scheduler keeps final authority.
maria: that's more or less Option C — hybrid soft-credit. Adapter gets X soft credits per tenant per epoch; scheduler can reclaim via RPC when contended. Reclaim path must be non-blocking.
jessica: reclaim RPC latency is important. If reclaim takes 10-50ms we might have already scheduled the batch. Maybe we need an explicit fast path: scheduler flips a boolean on hot lanes and adapters stop prefetching new ones.
lee: or embed a lightweight lease token in the request envelope: adapter attaches lease_id, scheduler returns lease_valid_until. When near expiry adapter stops building new prefetched batches.
ankur: lease token approach sounds promising. Simpler to reason about than async revokes. But how to surface observability? We need metrics: soft_credit_used, lease_expiry_misses, prefetch_evictions.
maria: agreed. Also consider the cost model: adapter prefetching increases GPU effective utilization but raises tail latency for small requests if we misallocate. We should expose a config like:
```
adapter_config:
  soft_credit_per_tenant: 2
  soft_credit_refresh_ms: 200
  max_prefetch_coalesce_ms: 8
```
lee: nice. Also add `lease_granularity_ms` and `lease_renew_rpc_timeout_ms`. Keep knobs conservative by default.
oliver: another trade: where to place priority aging? If adapter queues requests by local timestamp, we might delay priority inversion signals to scheduler. Better to send priority hints along with admission tokens so scheduler can reorder on global view.
jessica: yes — the adapter should send `priority_hint` and `enqueue_ts`. Scheduler can decide when to promote. Don't let local ordering be authoritative.
ankur: related: KV cache affinity. If adapter moves requests across lanes to chase throughput, we lose KV locality. Maybe we need a lane affinity hint so scheduler can bind microbatches to a lane with warm cache.
maria: agreed. So message envelope becomes: `{tenant, priority_hint, enqueue_ts, lease_id?, lane_affinity_hint, estimated_tokens}`. Keep it minimal.
lee: operationally we need fallbacks: if adapter-scheduler protocol breaks (latency or RPC failure), adapter must still be able to service requests in degraded mode: single-request passthrough or local microbatching with strict latency cap.
ankur: add feature-flag gating for degraded behavior. Also add a small synthetic load test to validate degraded path doesn't explode GPUs.
jessica: next steps? I can write a short RFC fragment with Options A/B/C + lease proto + metrics + observability dashboards. We should also add a small PoC to validate lease validity semantics (renew vs revoke).
maria: please do. Also @lee can you model expected revocation frequency with current tenant traces? A quick sim will help pick default soft_credit_per_tenant.
lee: on it, will run a 24h sim against recent production traces.
oliver: I'll prototype the lease token envelope and a tiny in-memory adapter in the runtime sandbox.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-sandbox/adapters:prototype-lease v0.1 -> staging at 5043219890 by oliver
maria: thanks all — sync in tomorrow eng-runtime sync if we have early results. :thumbsup:
